title: The Argument for Traveling More Slowly
summaryZh: 作者反思把旅行當成景點清單的習慣，主張用較少移動與較長停留換取更深的理解，同時承認慢遊並非人人可行。

sentences.text: I used to plan trips by opening a map and asking how many famous places I could connect in the fewest days.
sentences.zh: 我以前規劃旅行時，會打開地圖，問自己能在最少天數內串起多少知名景點。

sentences.text: The resulting schedules looked efficient, which is another way of saying they left no room for reality.
sentences.zh: 排出的行程看似有效率，換個方式說，就是完全沒有替現實留下空間。

sentences.text: A delayed train felt like a stolen museum, and an unexpected conversation became an obstacle to the next reservation.
sentences.zh: 火車誤點像是偷走了一間博物館，一場意外的談話則成了趕往下一個預約的障礙。

sentences.text: I was collecting evidence that I had traveled while repeatedly refusing the conditions that make travel interesting.
sentences.zh: 我不斷收集自己旅行過的證據，卻一再拒絕那些讓旅行變有趣的條件。

sentences.text: My habits changed after I spent ten days in a coastal town because a regional rail strike canceled my onward journey.
sentences.zh: 一次區域鐵路罷工取消了後續行程，迫使我在海邊小鎮待上十天，也改變了我的習慣。

sentences.text: At first, the extra days seemed empty because I had already visited everything the guidebook considered important.
sentences.zh: 起初，多出的日子顯得空洞，因為旅遊書認為重要的地方我都去過了。

sentences.text: Then repetition began doing what novelty could not: it made small differences visible.
sentences.zh: 接著，重複開始做到新奇做不到的事：讓細微差異變得可見。

sentences.text: I noticed which bakery sold out before noon, when fishing boats returned, and how the main square changed after commuters left.
sentences.zh: 我注意到哪間麵包店中午前就售罄、漁船何時回港，以及通勤者離開後主廣場如何改變。

sentences.text: None of those observations qualified as attractions, yet together they gave the town a shape I could remember.
sentences.zh: 這些觀察沒有一項算得上景點，但合在一起，卻讓小鎮有了我能記住的輪廓。

sentences.text: Slow travel is often advertised as morally superior, but that claim deserves some resistance.
sentences.zh: 慢速旅行常被宣傳成道德上更優越的選擇，但這種說法值得質疑。

sentences.text: Long stays can require flexible work, money, and secure documents, all of which are distributed unevenly.
sentences.zh: 長期停留可能需要彈性工作、金錢與穩定的旅行證件，而這些條件的分配並不均等。

sentences.text: Someone with five vacation days is not shallow for wanting to see more than one place.
sentences.zh: 只有五天假期的人想多看一個地方，並不代表他很膚淺。

sentences.text: The useful principle is not that every journey must be long, but that constant movement has a cost worth noticing.
sentences.zh: 有用的原則不是每趟旅程都必須很長，而是持續移動有一種值得注意的代價。

sentences.text: Each transfer consumes attention, creates another chance for delay, and keeps part of the mind focused on departure.
sentences.zh: 每次轉乘都會消耗注意力、增加延誤的機會，並讓部分心思始終放在離開上。

sentences.text: Now I remove one destination from nearly every first draft and give the remaining places the recovered time.
sentences.zh: 如今，幾乎每份初版行程我都會刪掉一個目的地，把省下的時間留給其他地方。

sentences.text: I return with fewer photographs, but the places in them feel less like backgrounds and more like places where life occurred.
sentences.zh: 我帶回的照片變少了，但照片中的地方不再只是背景，而更像是真有生活發生過的所在。

questions.q: What changed the writer's approach to travel?
options: A rail strike forced a longer stay in one town
A friend refused to follow the original schedule

questions.q: Why does the writer resist calling slow travel morally superior?
options: Slow travel always produces more pollution
The ability to stay longer depends on privileges not everyone has
Local residents generally dislike long term visitors

questions.q: What practical rule does the writer now follow?
options: Visit every major attraction before relaxing
Remove one destination and spend longer in the others
